hero.lead: An oil state of 4.9 million with one of the world’s oldest sovereign wealth funds, which returned to bond markets in 2025 and raised $6 billion more in July 2026 as the war in the region cut exports.

capital.heading: A wealth fund nation that borrows again.

record.text: Three-tranche sovereign bonds of 3, 5 and 10 years, July 2026
Three-part dollar bond, October 2025: the first since 2017
Borrowing ceiling under the 2025 debt law, with maturities up to 50 years
General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025

register.name: Treasury bonds and public debt tawarruq, 7 years
register.detail: Central Bank of Kuwait for the Ministry of Finance · competitive auction · uniform yield 4.125% · announced 28 October 2026
register.note: One of seven public debt issuance announcements from 20 May to 28 October 2026, with tenors of 2 to 7 years
register.text: Kuwaiti dinar treasury bonds and public debt tawarruq, the sharia-compliant form, issued by the Central Bank of Kuwait on behalf of the Ministry of Finance in a competitive auction at a uniform yield of 4.125%. Domestic issues of this kind, made under the public debt law of March 2025, raise local-currency finance for the state budget, which carries the public services behind the seven standards.

register.name: Sovereign bonds, three tranches
register.detail: State of Kuwait, acting through the Ministry of Finance · $3bn three-year, $1.5bn five-year and $1.5bn ten-year bonds · July 2026
register.note: Priced at 70, 75 and 85 basis points over US Treasuries; orders above $18 billion
register.text: Three tranches of US dollar bonds of 3, 5 and 10 years, sold by the State of Kuwait in July 2026 under the public debt law of March 2025, which set a ceiling of KD 30 billion with maturities of up to 50 years. They finance the state budget, which carries the public services behind the seven standards.

register.name: Return to the dollar bond market
register.detail: State of Kuwait, acting through the Ministry of Finance · $3.25bn three-year, $3bn five-year and $5bn ten-year bonds · October 2025
register.note: Kuwait’s first US dollar issue since 2017; priced at 40, 40 and 50 basis points over US Treasuries
register.text: Three tranches of US dollar bonds of 3, 5 and 10 years, sold by the State of Kuwait in October 2025, its return to international markets under the public debt law of March 2025. They finance the state budget, which carries the public services behind the seven standards.

register.name: Az-Zour North Phase 2 and 3 water and power plant
register.detail: Kuwait Authority for Partnership Projects and the Ministry of Electricity, Water and Renewable Energy with ACWA Power and Gulf Investment Corporation · build-own-operate-transfer, 25-year concession · signed 10 August 2025
register.note: Awarded through a competitive tender under the public-private partnership framework; Gulf Investment Corporation holds an effective 16%
register.text: A public-private partnership to build and run a plant of about 2,700 megawatts of electricity and 120 million gallons of water a day, awarded by competitive tender and implemented on a build-own-operate-transfer model with a 25-year concession. It adds power and desalinated water in a desert nation, which serve the energy and water standards.
by: Ministry of Electricity, Water and Renewable Energy

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.label: Of GDP from oil and gas rents, 2020
items.text: Oil rents near a third of the economy, and reserves to last for generations.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 18% are under fifteen: a young citizen workforce for an economy beyond oil.

items.name: The Debt Ceiling
items.label: Borrowing authority over 50 years, 2025 law
items.text: Room to finance a generation of investment at long maturities, alongside the wealth fund.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: A small farmed area in the desert, irrigated with care.

items.name: GreenLife
items.text: A Kuwaiti company that runs Kuwait’s first commercial aeroponic farm, growing leafy greens without soil all year with 96% less water than field farming; its first phase of 7,500 m² produces 800 to 900 kg of Lollo lettuce and 600 to 700 kg of iceberg lettuce a day, and a second phase of 16,500 m² was announced in 2025.

items.name: Dawraty
items.text: A Kuwait-based company whose bilingual, AI-powered learning platform lets institutions deliver and track accredited education in healthcare, professional certification and exam preparation, with Kuwait University among its partners, across Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain and Jordan; in September 2026 it raised a $2 million seed round backed by Qatar Development Bank.

items.name: Fawzia Al Sultan Healthcare Network (FSHN)
items.text: A non-profit network in Kuwait that provides physiotherapy, speech, occupational and behavioural therapy and mental health care, with fees set for each treatment plan and employee assistance programmes, while children from low-income families usually receive treatment free or at a highly reduced cost, about 70% of them through sponsorships.

items.name: Dawi
items.text: A Kuwaiti digital health platform of the company Fresh Minds, booked through its website or mobile app, that connects patients with hospitals, clinics and doctors for appointments, online consultations and second opinions; in March 2026 it agreed with the Supreme Council for Family Affairs to offer free psychological support and counselling sessions to people facing stress from the conditions in Kuwait and the region.

items.name: 312 Café
items.text: Kuwait’s first café staffed entirely by people with disabilities, in Salmiya, named after 3 December, the International Day of Persons with Disabilities; it has partnered with institutions such as the British Embassy in Kuwait.
